title: Visibility Fabric for Cross-Team Dependency Chronicles
creator: Ananya Rao
description: Create a lightweight, auditable 'visibility fabric' that captures dependency signals across Engineering, Design, Security, and Infra to power roadmap readiness scoring and automated escalation workflows. The fabric should surface unambiguous ownership, earliest-blocker dates, contingency plans, and an opt-in telemetry pipe into Console readiness dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Dependency record model available in Roadmap Orchestration with standardized fields (owner, blocker_status, earliest_blocker_date, contingency, signal_quality)
A2: UI in Console showing a team-agnostic dependency timeline and readiness score for each initiative page
A3: Notifications created for 'readiness regressions' when a dependency's earliest_blocker_date slips > 3 business days
A4: Minimal CSV/JSON export and webhook endpoint so partner teams can consume signals
A5: Pilot run with 3 cross-functional initiatives (Serving Runtime, Dedicated Autoscaling, Private Deployments) with feedback logged
progress_updates: 2026-02-09: Kickoff with Eng (runtime owners), Design, Security, and Infra. Agreed to align on 6 canonical dependency fields; product to draft schema.
2026-02-18: Prototype schema v0.1 reviewed. Security requested explicit 'data_classification' and 'kms_owner' fields for any dependency touching customer data.
2026-02-23: Decided to store minimal signals in Roadmap DB and push richer details to Confluence links to avoid schema bloat. Trade-off: fewer structured fields vs quicker adoption.
2026-03-03: Console devs built a read-only mock of the dependency timeline. UX feedback: need clearer differentiation between 'soft' and 'hard' blockers.

2026-03-08: Pilot selection complete: runtime-batching-improvement (ENG-2399), dedicated-autoscaler-config (ENG-3010), private-onprem-package (ENG-3122). PMs for each initiative agreed to participate.
decisions: D1: Use a small canonical set of fields (owner, blocker_type, severity, earliest_blocker_date, contingency, signal_origin) rather than capturing freeform text fields to allow algorithmic scoring.
D2: Readiness score will be calculated weekly using a heuristic that weights blocker severity and signal freshness; exact formula to be iterated after pilot.
D3: Automations (alerts/webhooks) will be opt-in per initiative to respect teams who want manual workflows during early adoption.
D4: Security-approved the schema only if 'data_classification' exists and if any KMS integrations are documented in the dependency record.
open_risks: R1: Adoption risk - teams may not keep dependency fields updated unless Console shows immediate value (we need quick wins in the UI)
R2: Ambiguity risk - inconsistent interpretation of 'earliest_blocker_date' across teams could corrupt readiness calculations
R3: Integration risk - some infra teams expose data via private trackers which require permissioning to hook into the visibility fabric
R4: Over-automation risk - too many alerts may cause alert fatigue; we need sensible defaults and throttling
next_steps: NS1: Finalize schema v0.2 with security and infra additions by 2026-03-14
NS2: Console team to implement a 'dependency tile' component and connect to Roadmap DB read endpoints (ETA 3 sprints)
NS3: Run pilot onboarding sessions with initiative PMs and assign liaisons in Eng/Design/Security for each pilot
NS4: Define readiness score formula and create synthetic backfill for historical initiatives to validate signal quality
stakeholders: Rahul Mehta (Eng - Serving Runtime) - pilot tech lead
